minutes.headline: School Committee capped the extended day program at 80 primary and 60 Turkey Hill, and approved girls ice hockey and swim co-ops.
minutes.summary: The committee heard activity and athletic fee comparisons and approved two co-op teams, a hockey trip, an extended day enrollment cap for safety and space, superintendent and committee goals, donations, and initial approval of a Quebec trip. It pulled policy 6505 back to subcommittee. A resident proposed that savings from teacher turnover be returned to the town.

what_happened.line: The School Committee capped the extended day program at 80 children at the primary school and 60 at Turkey Hill, citing safety and space.
The committee accepted girls ice hockey and swim co-ops with Leominster, after hearing that costs are split among participants through a user fee and ice time assessment.
It approved the Waterville Valley hockey trip and gave initial approval to a Quebec trip.
Policy 6505 and 6501 went back to the policy subcommittee; second reading was waived for policies 1202, 1700 and 2200.
The committee approved its goals as presented and a line-item transfer for a tractor before snow season; a resident asked that teacher turnover savings go back to the town.

why_it_matters: The extended day cap limits how many families can get before- and after-school care, and a message to parents was due the next day.
The new co-op teams and athletic fee discussion bear on what families pay to play, since costs are shared among participants through user fees.
The Quebec trip costs families about a thousand dollars per student as heard, and it has only initial approval so far.
watch_next: Final approval of the Quebec trip, which received only initial approval at this meeting.
Policy 6505 and 6501 returning from the policy subcommittee for another reading.
